title: Performance: where compiled code wins and how it was measured
summary: Gains come from not tokenising, routing calls directly, and the IBM REXX/370 compiler's techniques (Tom Dyer's brief): stems as arrays, loop counters as machine integers, whole-number operators on int64, native registers. Tight-loop bench native/bench/loops.rex: 4.49 s to 0.26 s compiled against 1.55 s interpreted. The compiler compiling itself: native 217 s, interpreted 300 s (fixed point at abdae83). Josep Maria Blasco's Rexx Parser benchmark (pbench2.rex) compiled: dump pass 40.8 s interpreted against 19.3 s compiled, three passes 127.6 s against 55.4 s (2.3x), dumps identical; his own rebuild at ca25535 was identical over 171,372 elements. Crossings (calls between compiled code and the interpreter) dominate when compiled code works on interpreter objects: count them before optimising.
invariants: Every fast path keeps the interpreter's results byte for byte; it checks its case at run time and otherwise falls back.
Time on an idle machine, one build or run at a time; report interpreted and compiled side by side.
Report numbers with the commit they were measured on.
